title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the neighbouring pages. Grothendieck works with an abstract 'atelier' (workshop) for analysis situs. It consists of a set M of 'lieux' (loci), ordered by two relations ≤ and ≪, together with a subset L ↪ M. 'Figures' F are objects of a class 𝓕. Each figure has a set of strata F̃ ⊂ M (page 5 calls it the 'diplôme' of F, a doubtful reading).

Two maps were defined on page 5, by pulling back along L ↪ M:
- omb : 𝓕 → 𝔓(L), the shadow (ombre) of F.
- multomb : 𝓕 → Fig(L), the multishadow (multiombre) of F.
The first map need not be injective; the second 'tends to be'.

This page explains the definitions.
- Shadow. omb(F) is the set of loci of L that meet F. These are called the loci 'of the figure'. They are not to be confused with the strata of F, which are also loci.
- Multishadow. multomb(F) is the family (omb(S))_{S∈F̃} of the shadows of the strata. It is indexed by F̃ and is a 'set-theoretic figure' in L.
- Incidence. The incidence relation of this set-theoretic figure is exactly the incidence relation between strata of F. That is the order on F̃ induced by ≤ on M. A parenthesis compares this with ≪, which apparently reduces to equality there (reading uncertain).
- Reconstruction contrast. Figures are practically never recoverable from their shadow alone. In the case of 'set-theoretic workshops' (ateliers ensemblistes) they are recoverable from their multishadow. This is promised for later ('Nous y reviendrons').

The section then turns (§) to the canonical order relations ≤, ≪, ≼ on 𝓕. Page 7 gives these the names sub-figure, refinement and subdivision.

In modern terms: a stratified object is replaced by its poset of strata together with the trace of each stratum on a set of 'points' L. In the set-theoretic model, a stratified subset (a partition of a subset into strata with a closure/incidence order) is determined by the family of its strata as subsets. Its face poset is the induced incidence order. Purpose: to set up the basic combinatorial vocabulary (shadows, incidence, order relations among figures) for an axiomatic 'tame topology' / analysis situs.
errors: No mathematical error. The reconstruction claim is only asserted for set-theoretic workshops and deferred ('Nous y reviendrons'). In the set-theoretic case it is essentially tautological: a stratified set is the family of its strata. In general multomb need not be injective, as page 5 already admits ('a une tendance à l'être').

The parenthesis '(ou par ≪ au choix, se réduisant au =)' is ambiguous. If ≪ restricted to strata reduces to equality, then ≪ cannot define the same incidence relation as ≤. Most likely it means that ≪ is NOT the relevant relation, or that it induces only the trivial order.

ideas.what: Shadow of a figure: the set of points/loci meeting it; multishadow: the family of shadows of its strata, indexed by the strata poset
ideas.modern_name: Support / trace of a stratified set; family of strata as subsets (face poset with its realization)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather); poset-of-strata viewpoint e.g. Lurie's exit paths, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 announces 'topologie modérée' and dévissage of stratified structures, but not this vocabulary

ideas.what: Incidence relation of strata = order on F̃ induced by ≤ on loci
ideas.modern_name: Poset of strata / closure (frontier) order of a stratification
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (tame topology section) discusses stratified spaces in general terms

ideas.what: Figures are not recoverable from their shadow but are recoverable from their multishadow in 'set-theoretic workshops'
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity of the map from stratified subsets to their families of strata

missed.claim: The 'atelier' axiomatics, with loci M, points L ⊂ M, figures with strata, and shadow/multishadow maps, is an unpublished attempt at an axiomatic tame topology. The general reconstruction question (when is multomb injective outside the set-theoretic case?) is explicitly deferred. Its content here is elementary; only the framework itself is of archival interest.
missed.quote: elles se reconstituent pourtant (cas des "ateliers ensemblistes") à partir de sa multiombre. Nous y reviendrons.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. It documents Grothendieck's 1986 vocabulary for tame topology, which could be compared with o-minimal structures and with poset-stratified spaces (exit-path ∞-categories). No new theorem is on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: Definitional and expository page in a private axiomatic framework. The ideas (shadow, strata incidence poset, reconstruction from strata) are elementary and standard in substance. Only the terminology is unpublished.
transcription_corrections: Line 'la relation d'[-...-] incidence[?] de la figure ensembliste': in the image, the word after 'd'' is struck out and followed by 'de la / figure ensembliste'. 'incidence' is not clearly written there; it appears only in the next line ('la relation d'incidence entre strates').
'(ou par ≪ au choix, se réduisant au =)' is uncertain. The handwriting may read '(non par ≪ ..., se réduisant au =)', i.e. ≪ induces only equality on the strata.
'à partir de sa multiombre' is more likely 'de leur multiombre' (plural antecedent 'les figures'), though the handwriting is compressed.
'Ainsi' at the start: the 'A' is overwritten (corrected capital).
